deities: Lord Siddheshwar (Shiva; the main Shiva Linga in the sanctum)
68 Shiva lingams installed by Shri Siddharameshwar in the main courtyard (including the Amrit/immortality Linga)
Marble samadhi of Shri Siddharameshwar at the centre of the temple (he attained samadhi here in 1167 AD)
Idolic effigy of Shri Siddharameshwar within the sanctum of the main temple
Lord Ganesha (small temple in the complex)
Lord Vithoba (Vitthala) and Goddess Rukmini (small temples in the complex)
festivals: Makar Sankranti Yatra (mid-January, 3 days: Bhogi, Sankrant, Kinkrant) — the famous Nandi Dhwaja procession celebrating the symbolic wedding of the saint's Yoga Danda with the Kumbhar Kanya, followed by Akshata Sohala and Homa
Gadda Yatra / Gadda Jatra (15-day fair around the temple during Makar Sankranti)

history.dynasty: Yadava period (Hemadpanti architecture; Chalukya influences); administered since 1899 by the Shri Siddheshwar Devsthan Panch Committee
history.period: 12th century CE (Shri Siddharameshwar attained samadhi in 1167 AD)
history.summary: The Shri Siddheshwar Temple in Solapur is the gramdaivat (guardian deity) shrine of the city, dedicated to Siddheshwar — the 12th-century Lingayat saint Shri Siddharameshwar, a yogi and devotee of Shri Mallikarjuna of Srisailam, who is venerated as a god in the Lingayat (Veerashaiva) faith and counted as one of its five prophets. Born to Muddanna and Suggaladevi, he was part of the 12th-century Sharana movement and preached the teachings of Basavanna; tradition credits him with composing 68,000 vachanas in Kannada. As Solapur was drought-prone, he had a lake dug with the help of devotees (the Siddheshwar lake on whose island the temple stands) to solve the city's drinking water problem. He built the temple and installed 68 Shiva lingams in and around it as per his guru's instructions, consecrating also the Ashtavinayak shrines in the Panchkroshi of Solapur. The temple and lake have been administered since 1899 by the Shri Siddheshwar Devsthan Panch Committee. Built in Hemadpanti style, the complex includes the saint's marble samadhi at its centre, a silver-plated Nandi, and smaller shrines of Ganesha, Vithoba and Rukmini.

name: Shri Siddheshwar Temple
town_description: Solapur is a city and municipal corporation in south-eastern Maharashtra, near the Karnataka border, and the administrative headquarters of Solapur district. It is a melting pot of Marathi, Telugu and Kannada cultures, a major railway junction on the north-south line, and a centre of textile industry famous for Solapuri chaddars (bed-sheets). The city is dominated by its gramdaivat, Shri Siddheshwar, whose temple stands on an island in the Siddheshwar lake beneath the walls of the Bhuikot Fort; nearby pilgrim centres include Pandharpur (Vithoba) and Akkalkot (Swami Samarth Math).

travel.airport: Solapur Airport, the nearest airport (approx. 7-18 km from the temple; verify — sources vary). Pune International Airport is approx. 235-260 km away.
travel.railway: Solapur Junction, the nearest railway station (approx. 2-4 km from the temple; verify), well connected to Mumbai, Pune, Hyderabad and other major cities.
travel.road: Solapur is a major transport hub well connected by road: Pune is approx. 235 km (about 5 hours via NH65), Mumbai approx. 467 km; regular state and private buses run to Solapur, and autos/taxis ply to the temple within the city.

visitor_information.best_time: Makar Sankranti (mid-January) for the grand Yatra and Nandi Dhwaja procession; Maha Shivaratri (February-March); October to March for pleasant weather (15-25°C). Early mornings or late evenings are best for peaceful darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Generally 5:00 AM to about 9:00 PM daily (verify — sources list 5 AM–9 PM, 5 AM–10:30 PM, and 6 AM–7 PM). Entry is free. Traditional dress code: men in dhoti, women in saree or other traditional attire. Anna prasadam (lunch/dinner) is served to devotees.
